plan: 1 Chronicles 29:23-25; 2 Chronicles 1:1; 1 Kings 2:13-46; 1 Kings 3:1-4; 2 Chronicles 1:2-6; 1 Kings 3:5-15; 2 Chronicles 1:7-13; Psalm 83:1-18

readings.title: Solomon Ascends the Throne
readings.subtitle: All Israel submits to the new king, and his reign is established.
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 29:23] And Shelomoh sat on the throne of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> as sovereign instead of Daviḏ his father, and prospered; and all Yisra’ěl obeyed him. [24] And all the rulers and the mighty men, and also all the sons of Sovereign Daviḏ, submitted themselves to Shelomoh the sovereign. [25] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> exalted <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh exceedingly in the eyes of all Yisra’ěl, and put upon him such royal splendour as had not been on any sovereign before him in Yisra’ěl. [2 Chronicles 1:1] And Shelomoh son of Daviḏ was strengthened in his reign, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> was with <dn>את</dn> him and exalted him exceedingly.

readings.title: Adonijah's Fatal Request
readings.subtitle: Through Bathsheba, Adonijah asks for Abishag, sealing his own doom.
readings.text: [1 Kings 2:13] And Aḏoniyahu son of Ḥaggith came to Bathsheḇa the mother of Shelomoh, and she said, “Do you come in peace?” And he said, “Peace.” [14] And he said, “<dn>I</dn> have a word for you,” and she said, “Speak.” [15] And he said, “You know that the reign was mine, and all Yisra’ěl had set their faces toward me, that <dn>I</dn> should reign. But the reign has been turned around, and has become my brother’s, for it was his from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [16] “And now, <dn>I</dn> am making one request of you, do not refuse me.” And she said to him, “Say it.” [17] And he said, “Please speak to Sovereign Shelomoh – for he would not refuse you – to give me <dn>את</dn> Aḇishaḡ the Shunammite as wife.” [18] And Bathsheḇa said, “Good, let me speak for you to the sovereign.” [19] And Bathsheḇa came to Sovereign Shelomoh, to speak to him for Aḏoniyahu. And the sovereign rose up to meet her and bowed down to her, and sat down on his throne and had a throne set for the sovereign’s mother. So she sat at his right hand. [20] And she said, “<dn>I</dn> am making one small request of you, do not refuse me.” And the sovereign said to her, “Ask it, my mother, for <dn>I</dn> do not refuse you.” [21] Then she said, “Let Aḇishaḡ the Shunammite be given to Aḏoniyahu your brother as wife.” [22] And Sovereign Shelomoh answered and said to his mother, “Now why do you ask <dn>את</dn> Aḇishaḡ the Shunammite for Aḏoniyahu? Ask for him <dn>את</dn> the reign also – for he is my older brother – for him, and for Eḇyathar the priest, and for Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah.” [23] And Sovereign Shelomoh swore by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “<dn>Elohim</dn> does so to me, and more also, if Aḏoniyahu has not spoken <dn>את</dn> this word against his own life! [24] “And now, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, who established me and set me on the throne of Daviḏ my father, and who has made me a house, as <dn>He</dn> promised, Aḏoniyahu shall be put to death today!” [25] And Sovereign Shelomoh sent by the hand of Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa, and he fell upon him, and he died.

readings.title: The Dismissal of Abiathar and Execution of Joab
readings.subtitle: Solomon removes the disloyal priest and commander, fulfilling prophecy and David's command.
readings.text: [1 Kings 2:26] Then the sovereign said to Eḇyathar the priest, “Go to Anathoth, to your own fields, for you deserve death. But <dn>I</dn> do not put you to death at this time, because you did bear <dn>את</dn> the ark of the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> before my father Daviḏ, and because you were afflicted in all <dn>את</dn> my father was afflicted in.” [27] So Shelomoh dismissed Eḇyathar from being priest to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to fill <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> spoke concerning the house of Ěli at Shiloh. [28] And news came to Yo’aḇ, for Yo’aḇ had turned aside after Aḏoniyah, though he did not turn aside after Aḇshalom. And Yo’aḇ fled to the Tent of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and took hold of the horns of the slaughter-place. [29] And the report came to Sovereign Shelomoh that Yo’aḇ had fled to the Tent of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and see, he is by the slaughter-place. Then Shelomoh sent Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa, saying, “Go, fall on him.” [30] So Benayahu came to the Tent of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said to him, “Thus said the sovereign, ‘Come out!’ ” And he said, “No, for here <dn>I</dn> die.” And Benayahu brought back word to the sovereign, saying, “Thus said Yo’aḇ, and thus he answered me.” [31] And the sovereign said to him, “Do as he has said, and fall upon him. And you shall bury him, so that you take away from me and from the house of my father <dn>את</dn> the blood which Yo’aḇ shed without cause. [32] “Thus <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall return <dn>את</dn> his blood on his head, because he had fallen on two men more righteous and better than he, and killed them with the sword, while my father Daviḏ did not know it: Aḇněr son of Něr, commander of the army of Yisra’ěl, and Amasa son of Yether, commander of the army of Yehuḏah. [33] “So shall their blood return upon the head of Yo’aḇ and upon the head of his seed forever. But upon Daviḏ and his seed, upon his house and his throne, there is to be peace forever from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [34] Then Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa went up and fell upon him and put him to death. And he was buried in his own house in the wilderness. [35] And the sovereign put <dn>את</dn> Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa in his place over the army, and the sovereign put <dn>את</dn> Tsaḏoq the priest in the place of Eḇyathar.

readings.title: Shimei's Transgression and Execution
readings.subtitle: By leaving Jerusalem, Shimei violates his oath and is put to death, securing Solomon's throne.
readings.text: [1 Kings 2:36] And the sovereign sent and called for Shim‛i, and said to him, “Build yourself a house in Yerushalayim and dwell there, and do not go out from there anywhere. [37] “And it shall be, on the day you go out and pass over <dn>את</dn> the wadi Qiḏron, know for certain that you shall die – your blood is on your own head.” [38] And Shim‛i said to the sovereign, “The word is good. As my master the sovereign has said, so your servant does.” So Shim‛i dwelt in Yerushalayim many days. [39] And it came to be at the end of three years, that two slaves of Shim‛i fled to Aḵish son of Ma‛aḵah, sovereign of Gath. And they informed Shim‛i, saying, “See, your slaves are in Gath!” [40] And Shim‛i rose up, and saddled his donkey, and went to Aḵish at Gath to look for <dn>את</dn> his slaves. And Shim‛i went and brought <dn>את</dn> his slaves from Gath. [41] And Shelomoh was told that Shim‛i had gone from Yerushalayim to Gath and had come back. [42] So the sovereign sent and called for Shim‛i, and said to him, “Did <dn>I</dn> not make you swear by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and warn you, saying, ‘Know for certain that on the day you leave to go anywhere, you shall certainly die’? And you said to me, ‘The word <dn>I</dn> have heard is good.’ [43] “And why have you not guarded <dn>את</dn> the oath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> the command that <dn>I</dn> gave you?” [44] The sovereign also said to Shim‛i, “You shall know <dn>את</dn> all the evil that your heart has known, that you did to my father Daviḏ. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall return <dn>את</dn> your evil on your own head. [45] “But Sovereign Shelomoh is blessed, and the throne of Daviḏ is established before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> forever.” [46] So the sovereign commanded Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa, and he went out and fell on him, and he died. And the reign was established in the hand of Shelomoh.

readings.title: Solomon's Marriage and Worship at Gibeon
readings.subtitle: Solomon allies with Egypt and demonstrates his love for YeHoVaH by offering a thousand sacrifices.
readings.text: [1 Kings 3:1] And Shelomoh joined in marriage with Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim, and took <dn>את</dn> the daughter of Pharaoh, and brought her to the City of Daviḏ until he had completed building <dn>את</dn> his own house, and <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>את</dn> the wall all around Yerushalayim. [2] Only, the people slaughtered at the high places, for a house for the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had not been built until those days. [3] And Shelomoh loved <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, walking in the laws of his father Daviḏ, except that he slaughtered and burned incense at the high places. [4] And the sovereign went to Gib‛on to slaughter there, for that was the great high place. Shelomoh offered a thousand ascending offerings on that slaughter-place. [2 Chronicles 1:2] And Shelomoh spoke to all Yisra’ěl, to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and to the judges, and to every leader in all Yisra’ěl, the heads of the fathers’ houses. [3] And Shelomoh, and all the assembly with him, went to the high place that was at Gib‛on. For the Tent of Appointment of <dn>Elohim</dn> was there, which Mosheh the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had made in the wilderness. [4] But Daviḏ had brought up <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> from Qiryath Ye‛arim to the place Daviḏ had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it at Yerushalayim. [5] And <dn>את</dn> the bronze slaughter-place, which Betsal’ěl son of Uri, son of Ḥur, had made, he put before the Dwelling Place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>; and Shelomoh and the assembly sought it out. [6] And Shelomoh went up there to the bronze slaughter-place before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which was at the Tent of Appointment, and offered a thousand ascending offerings on it.

readings.title: The Dream at Gibeon
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH appears to Solomon and, pleased with his request for wisdom, promises him riches and honor as well.
readings.text: [1 Kings 3:5] At Gib‛on <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to Shelomoh in a dream by night, and <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“Ask what <dn>I</dn> should give you.”</dq> [6] And Shelomoh said, “<dn>You</dn> have shown great loving-commitment to your servant Daviḏ my father, as he walked before <dn>You</dn> in truth, and in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with <dn>You</dn>. And <dn>You</dn> have guarded for him this great loving-commitment, and did give him a son to sit on his throne, as it is this day. [7] “And now, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>You</dn> have set up <dn>Your</dn> servant to reign instead of my father Daviḏ. But <dn>I</dn> am a little child, <dn>I</dn> do not know how to go out or to come in. [8] “And <dn>Your</dn> servant is in the midst of <dn>Your</dn> people whom <dn>You</dn> have chosen, a great people, too numerous to be numbered or counted. [9] “Shall <dn>You</dn> then give to <dn>Your</dn> servant an understanding heart to rule <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> people, to discern between good and evil? For who is able to rule <dn>את</dn> this great people of <dn>Yours</dn>?” [10] And the word was good in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that Shelomoh had asked this. [11] So <dn>Elohim</dn> said to him, <dq>“Because you have asked <dn>את</dn> this, and have not asked long life for yourself, nor have asked riches for yourself, nor have asked <dn>את</dn> the life of your enemies, but have asked for yourself discernment to understand right-ruling,</dq> [12] <dq>see, <dn>I</dn> shall do according to your words. See, <dn>I</dn> shall give you a wise and understanding heart, so that there was none like you before you, and none like you shall arise after you.</dq> [13] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall also give you what you have not asked: both riches and esteem, so that there shall not be anyone like you among the sovereigns all your days.</dq> [14] <dq>And if you walk in <dn>My</dn> ways, to guard <dn>My</dn> laws and <dn>My</dn> commands, as your father Daviḏ walked, then <dn>I</dn> shall prolong your days.”</dq> [15] And Shelomoh awoke, and see, it was a dream! And he came into Yerushalayim and stood before <dn>את</dn> the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and offered up ascending offerings and made peace offerings. And he made a feast for all his servants. [2 Chronicles 1:7] In that night <dn>Elohim</dn> appeared to Shelomoh, and said to him, <dq>“Ask what <dn>I</dn> should give you.”</dq> [8] And Shelomoh said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “<dn>You</dn> have shown great loving-commitment to Daviḏ my father, and have made me reign in his place. [9] “Now, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, let <dn>Your</dn> promise to Daviḏ my father be steadfast, for <dn>You</dn> have made me reign over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth. [10] “Give me now wisdom and knowledge, that <dn>I</dn> might go out and come in before this people. For who is able to rule this great people of <dn>Yours</dn>?” [11] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Shelomoh, <dq>“Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked riches or wealth or esteem or <dn>את</dn> the life of your enemies, nor have you asked long life, but have asked wisdom and knowledge for yourself, to rule <dn>My</dn> people over whom <dn>I</dn> have made you sovereign,</dq> [12] <dq>wisdom and knowledge are given to you. And riches and wealth and esteem <dn>I</dn> give to you, such as none of the sovereigns have had who were before you, nor any after you is to have.”</dq> [13] And Shelomoh came from the high place that was at Gib‛on to Yerushalayim, from before the Tent of Appointment, and reigned over Yisra’ěl.

readings.subsection: A Prayer Against the Enemies of Israel
readings.title: A Confederacy Against Your People
readings.subtitle: The psalmist cries out to God as a coalition of nations conspires to destroy Israel.
readings.text: [Psalm 83:1] O <dn>Elohim</dn>, do not remain silent! Do not be speechless, And do not be still, O <dn>Ěl</dn>! [2] For look, <dn>Your</dn> enemies make an uproar, And those hating <dn>You</dn> have lifted up their head. [3] They craftily plot against <dn>Your</dn> people, And conspire against <dn>Your</dn> treasured ones. [4] They have said, “Come, And let us wipe them out as a nation, And let the name of Yisra’ěl be remembered no more.” [5] For they have conspired together with one heart; They have made a covenant against <dn>You</dn> – [6] The tents of Eḏom and the Yishma‛ělites, Mo’aḇ and the Haḡarites, [7] Geḇal, and Ammon, and Amalěq, Philistia with the inhabitants of Tsor, [8] Ashshur also has joined with them, They have helped the children of Lot. Selah.

readings.subsection: A Prayer Against the Enemies of Israel
readings.title: Let Them Know Your Name
readings.subtitle: A plea for God to defeat His enemies as in days of old, that they might be shamed and seek His name, YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [Psalm 83:9] Do to them as to Miḏyan, As to Sisera, As to Yaḇin at the wadi Qishon, [10] Who perished at Ěndor, Who became as dung for the ground. [11] Make their nobles like Orěḇ and like Ze’ěḇ, And all their princes like Zeḇaḥ and Tsalmunna, [12] Who have said, “Let us take possession of the pastures of <dn>Elohim</dn> For ourselves.” [13] O <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, make them as whirling dust, As stubble before the wind! [14] As a fire consumes a forest, And as a flame sets mountains on fire, [15] So pursue them with <dn>Your</dn> whirlwind, And frighten them with <dn>Your</dn> storm. [16] Fill their faces with shame, And let them seek <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> Name, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [17] Let them be ashamed and alarmed forever; And let them become abashed and perish, [18] And let them know that <dn>You</dn>, Whose Name is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> alone are the Most High over all the earth.
